use: Say you've had too much; chotto yopparatta is 'I'm a bit tipsy'.

example.romaji: chotto yopparatta kamo. mizu choudai.
example.ja: ちょっと酔っ払ったかも。水ちょうだい。
example.english: I might be a bit drunk. Can I have some water?

examplePolite.romaji: chotto yopparatte shimaimashita. omizu o kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: ちょっと酔っ払ってしまいました。お水をください。
examplePolite.english: I've had a bit too much. Could I have some water?

notes: yotta is a milder 'tipsy', and also means carsick or seasick.

english: that was fun; I had a great time
use: Say after a trip, party or day out; the usual answer to dou datta?

example.romaji: kyou wa honto ni tanoshikatta! mata ikou ne.
example.ja: 今日はほんとに楽しかった！また行こうね。
example.english: Today was so much fun! Let's go again.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa hontou ni tanoshikatta desu. mata ikimashou.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は本当に楽しかったです。また行きましょう。
examplePolite.english: I really enjoyed today. Let's go again.

notes: For a funny or interesting film or book, omoshirokatta fits better.

use: Ask about a trip, test, date or meal that's over; answer tanoshikatta, yokatta, or maa maa (so-so).

example.romaji: ryokou dou datta? tanoshikatta?
example.ja: 旅行どうだった？楽しかった？
example.english: How was the trip? Was it fun?

examplePolite.romaji: ryokou wa dou deshita ka? tanoshikatta desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 旅行はどうでしたか？楽しかったですか？
examplePolite.english: How was your trip? Did you enjoy it?

notes: dou desu ka asks about now; dou datta asks about something finished.

english: what's it like?; how's it going?
use: Ask for a quick impression of a place or thing, or how something is going; answer ii kanji (going well).

example.romaji: atarashii shigoto, donna kanji?
example.ja: 新しい仕事、どんな感じ？
example.english: How's the new job going?

examplePolite.romaji: atarashii oshigoto, donna kanji desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 新しいお仕事、どんな感じですか？

notes: kanji here is 'feel', not the Chinese characters.

english: that was interesting; that was fun; that was funny
use: For films, books, talks or anything that held your interest or made you laugh.

example.romaji: ano eiga, sugoku omoshirokatta yo.
example.ja: あの映画、すごく面白かったよ。
example.english: That movie was really good.

examplePolite.ja: あの映画、すごく面白かったです。

notes: omoshiroi is 'interesting' as much as 'funny'; for a fun event, tanoshikatta fits better.

use: Ask someone's opinion; answer X to omou (I think X) or sou omou.

example.romaji: kono fuku, dou omou? chotto hade kana.
example.ja: この服、どう思う？ちょっと派手かな。
example.english: What do you think of this outfit? Too loud?

examplePolite.romaji: kono fuku, dou omoimasu ka? chotto hade deshou ka.
examplePolite.ja: この服、どう思いますか？ちょっと派手でしょうか。
examplePolite.english: What do you think of this outfit? Is it a bit loud?

notes: Use dou (how), not nani (what): nani o omou? sounds wrong.

use: Fills the pause while you think, or softens a no; a long, falling uun often means the answer is no.

example.romaji: uun, dou shiyou kana. mada kimete nai.
example.ja: うーん、どうしようかな。まだ決めてない。
example.english: Hmm, what should I do? I haven't decided yet.

examplePolite.romaji: uun, dou shimashou ka ne. mada kimete imasen.
examplePolite.ja: うーん、どうしましょうかね。まだ決めていません。
examplePolite.english: Hmm, what to do. I haven't decided yet.

notes: Said short with a drop (ううん, also uun), it means no; un alone is yeah.

use: Agree with an opinion; sou omowanai is 'I don't think so'.

example.romaji: un, watashi mo sou omou.
example.ja: うん、私もそう思う。
example.english: Yeah, I think so too.

examplePolite.ja: はい、私もそう思います。

notes: Usually with mo: watashi mo sou omou, 'I think so too'.

english: well, who knows; come on, let's go
use: With a shrug it dodges a question you can't answer; said briskly it gets people moving.

example.romaji: saa, doko itta n darou. shiranai.
example.ja: さあ、どこ行ったんだろう。知らない。
example.english: Who knows where he went. No idea.

examplePolite.ja: さあ、ちょっとわかりませんね。

notes: A bare saa can sound dismissive; add chotto wakaranai to soften it.

english: hard to say; I can't really say
use: When you can't judge yet or won't commit; also for a feeling that's hard to put into words.

example.romaji: mada hajimatta bakari da kara, nantomo ienai na.
example.ja: まだ始まったばかりだから、なんとも言えないな。
example.english: It's only just started, so it's hard to say.

examplePolite.romaji: mada hajimatta bakari na node, nantomo iemasen.
examplePolite.ja: まだ始まったばかりなので、なんとも言えません。
examplePolite.english: It's only just started, so I can't really say.

notes: nantomo ienai aji, 'a taste you can't describe', is praise.

use: Tell someone to stop, from playful teasing to real danger.

example.romaji: chotto, yamete yo! kusuguttai!
example.ja: ちょっと、やめてよ！くすぐったい！
example.english: Hey, stop it! That tickles!

examplePolite.ja: すみません、それ、やめてください。

notes: yamero is the harsh command form you'll hear in dramas; yamete is softer and used by anyone.

use: Surprise or delight at something you see, like a view, a gift or food arriving.

example.romaji: waa, kirei! mite, umi ga mieru yo.
example.ja: わあ、きれい！見て、海が見えるよ。
example.english: Wow, beautiful! Look, you can see the sea.

examplePolite.romaji: waa, kirei desu ne! umi ga miemasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: わあ、きれいですね！海が見えますよ。
examplePolite.english: Wow, how beautiful! You can see the sea.

notes: uwaa leans toward shock or disgust; waa is usually pleasant.

use: An adult catching a child or pet misbehaving; playful between friends.

example.romaji: kora! sonna tokoro ni nobotcha dame!
example.ja: こら！そんなところに登っちゃダメ！
example.english: Hey! You can't climb up there!

notes: Don't use it to call adults; ooi is the neutral calling 'hey'.

use: Muttered in frustration when something goes wrong; in slang it also intensifies, as in kuso muzui (damn hard).

example.romaji: kuso, mata maketa! mou ikkai!
example.ja: クソ、また負けた！もう一回！
example.english: Damn, lost again! One more time!

notes: Literally 'dung'. Good to recognize, risky to say: it sounds harsh, especially from a learner.

english: what do you mean?; what's going on?
use: Ask someone to explain something confusing or surprising; said sharply, it demands an explanation.

example.romaji: e, chuushi? dou iu koto?
example.ja: え、中止？どういうこと？
example.english: Wait, cancelled? What do you mean?

examplePolite.romaji: e, chuushi desu ka? dou iu koto desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: え、中止ですか？どういうことですか？
examplePolite.english: Wait, it's cancelled? What do you mean?

notes: dou iu imi? asks only what a word or sentence means.

use: Ask when you've lost the thread, or play dumb about something you'd rather not discuss.

example.romaji: e, nan no hanashi? zenzen shiranai kedo.
example.ja: え、何の話？全然知らないけど。
example.english: Huh, what are you talking about? I've no idea.

examplePolite.romaji: e, nan no hanashi desu ka? zenzen shiranai n desu kedo.
examplePolite.ja: え、何の話ですか？全然知らないんですけど。
examplePolite.english: Huh, what are you talking about? I've no idea.

notes: Joining a group, ask nan no hanashi shiteru no? (what are you all talking about?).

english: what do you mean?; what are you talking about?
use: Asks what someone is referring to; often feigned innocence when accused of something.

example.romaji: nan no koto? watashi, nani mo shiranai yo.
example.ja: 何のこと？私、何も知らないよ。
example.english: What are you talking about? I don't know anything.

examplePolite.romaji: nan no koto desu ka? watashi wa nani mo shirimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 何のことですか？私は何も知りません。
examplePolite.english: What do you mean? I don't know anything.

notes: Close to nan no hanashi; nan no koto points at one thing someone mentioned.

english: what do you want?; what is it?
use: Asked when someone calls you or turns up; can sound curt depending on tone.

example.romaji: nanka you? ima chotto isogashii n da kedo.
example.ja: 何か用？今ちょっと忙しいんだけど。
example.english: What is it? I'm a bit busy right now.

examplePolite.romaji: nanika goyou desu ka? ima chotto isogashii n desu ga.
examplePolite.ja: 何かご用ですか？今ちょっと忙しいんですが。
examplePolite.english: Can I help you? I'm a bit busy right now.

notes: nanika you? is the same, a touch less blunt. Staff use the polite form to mean 'Can I help you?'.

english: no, I mean...; that's not what I meant
use: Correct a misunderstanding, then say what you actually meant.

example.romaji: sou ja nakute, ashita no hanashi da yo.
example.ja: そうじゃなくて、明日の話だよ。
example.english: No, I mean tomorrow.

examplePolite.romaji: sou ja nakute, ashita no hanashi desu.
examplePolite.ja: そうじゃなくて、明日の話です。

notes: In formal talk: sou de wa nakute.

use: Quick correction, often with a hand wave, when someone guesses or does it wrong.

example.romaji: chigau chigau, sotchi ja nakute kotchi!
example.ja: 違う違う、そっちじゃなくてこっち！
example.english: No, no, not that one, this one!

notes: Politely, a single iie, chigaimasu. chigau also means 'different'.
